items.title: Sonny Bono’s Widow Makes Pitch to Appeals Court in Cher Royalties Saga: ‘Ex-Wives Are Excluded’
items.summary:
The long-running legal fight between Sonny Bono ’s widow and Cher is still going — and now, Mary Bono is trying to get an appeals court to side with her on royalty splits  

Mary filed her opening appeal brief on Monday (Nov. 23) in litigation over the publishing royalties from Sonny & Cher ’s 1960s catalog, including hits like “I Got You Babe,” “The Beat Goes On” and “Baby Don’t Go.” The duo married in 1967 and divorced in 1978, and Sonny later remarried Mary before dying in a 1998 skiing accident.

Related 

Cher Spent $1M in Legal Bills Fighting Sonny Bono’s Widow. A Judge Says She Must Pay It Herself 

Chris Brown Agrees to Increase Child Support — For Now — to Ex Diamond in Bitter Custody Fight 

Rod Wave Indicted on Drug & Gun Charges for Items Allegedly Found in Car After Speeding Stop 

The divorce settlement between Sonny & Cher promised a 50-50 split of composition royalties left over after Sonny’s publishers collected a 30% share. But Mary began asserting in 2021 that she could stop paying Cher entirely under copyright law’s termination right, which allows intellectual property transfers to be voided after a decades-long period has elapsed. 

After years of litigation, a federal judge sided with Cher in 2024 by finding that copyright termination could not apply to the royalties in a divorce agreement, which is essentially just a financial contract. Mary is now telling the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals that this ruling was incorrect and “creates chaos regarding ownership interests of heirs.” 

Mary’s appellate brief, obtained by Billboard , argues that Sonny &…
items.t: Sonny Bono’s Widow Makes Pitch to Appeals Court in Cher Royalties Saga: ‘Ex-Wives Are Excluded’

items.title: U2, ATEEZ, Ella Langley & More: Highlights of This Week’s Billboard Charts
items.summary:
Tuesday is new Billboard chart day each week! As all charts update each Tuesday, here’s a look at highlights of the latest rankings, dated Nov. 28 and reflecting the Nov. 13-19 measurement week, according to data tracker Luminate.

Among this week’s chart stars are ATEEZ , U2 , Ella Langley , Mariah Carey and Wham!

ATEEZ and U2 reflect high-profile groups that have hit the Billboard 200 album chart’s upper reaches since earlier this decade and the 1980s, respectively. ATEEZ earns its fourth No. 1 on the list with the debut of GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6 . The act first led in December 2023 with THE WORLD EP.FIN: WILL .

Related 

ATEEZ Earn Fourth No. 1 on Billboard 200 With ‘GOLDEN HOUR : Part.6’ 

Meanwhile, U2 debuts at No. 4 on the Billboard 200 with Carnaval de Luz . The band notches its 14th top 10 set, dating to the No. 7 launch of The Joshua Tree (the first of U2’s eight leaders) on the April 4, 1987, chart. The albums above it that week? Six other classics, from No. 1 on down: Beastie Boys’ Licensed to Ill , Bon Jovi’s Slippery When Wet , Paul Simon’s Graceland , Bruce Hornsby & the Range’s The Way It Is , Janet Jackson’s Control and Genesis’ Invisible Touch .

U2 adds its second Billboard 200 top 10 this decade, following Songs of Surrender (No. 5, 2023). Upon that LP’s arrival, U2 became just the fourth group to have scored newly charted top 10s in the 1980s, ‘90s, 2000s, ‘10s and ‘20s, joining AC/DC, Def Leppard and Metallica.

items.title: Tidal Becomes First Streaming Service to Ban AI Music From Its Platform
items.summary:
Tidal announced Tuesday (Nov. 24) that AI-generated music will be banned entirely from the platform, beginning Dec. 9. This follows the company’s announcement in July that AI music had been demonetized and labeled , with requirements for distributors to label AI songs. Tidal says that it will remove any songs that distributors say were created solely with AI tools.

In a post on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), Tidal claimed that 94% of AI-badged tracks had come from Suno. The company also claimed in a blog post that as of Nov. 6, 60% of the songs that it had received daily were AI-generated, that 96% of AI-generated songs on its platform had received no streams over the last three months and that it had taken down 66,000 tracks from people it suspects are impersonating another artist. The company says that songs created with assistance from AI tools, but are not entirely AI-generated, will be allowed to remain on the platform.

Related 

How Each Music Listening Platform Is Treating AI Music (Updating) 

Chris Brown Agrees to Increase Child Support — For Now — to Ex Diamond in Bitter Custody Fight 

Rod Wave Indicted on Drug & Gun Charges for Items Allegedly Found in Car After Speeding Stop 

“If you make music, you should be able to put it on Tidal knowing it won’t be buried under tracks no one asked for, or copied by someone pretending to be you,” the blog post read.

Tidal’s statement also said that 43% of songs delivered to the platform over the last three months have been marked as AI and labeled with a badge. Labeling has been a big part of the…
items.t: Tidal Becomes First Streaming Service to Ban AI Music From Its Platform

items.title: The Big Moon talk the “endless madness” of 2026 and the “pinch me” moment of playing Brixton Academy
items.summary:
Ahead of their real “pinch me” moment of headlining London’s iconic Brixton Academy, The Big Moon have spoken to NME about their year of “eternal, infinite, endless madness” and a new mindset shaped by overcoming illness and the magic of motherhood.

The date in the capital will cap off the band’s UK tour victory lap for acclaimed fourth album ‘Forever’. The honour of stepping onto the hallowed Brixton Academy stage was not lost on them.

“I can’t believe we are playing there,” singer Jules Jackson told NME . “I have so so so many happy memories of being at shows in that building since I was a teenager. I’m pinching myself. I can’t wait to yell along to our songs with everyone.”

Have they any surprises up their sleeves for the show?

“We have a load of new stage props which weve never had before,” Jackson replied. “So the show is going to be slick as hell. I’m hoping for high drama. It’s been so fun planning it out. Also some incredible lights which we are hoping will transport us into the galaxy.”

The Big Moon, 2026. Credit: Melanie Lehmann

items.title: Stevie Wonder addresses conspiracy theory that he’s not really blind: “Get in the car with me and we’ll see”
items.summary:
Stevie Wonder has poked fun at the long-standing conspiracy theory that he is not really blind during a show in Chicago – see footage below.

The legendary singer-songwriter was performing at the city’s United Center on Saturday (November 21) when he took a break between songs to address the rumours about his eyesight.

Speaking from behind his piano, he offered a joking challenge to those who believe the conspiracy theory. “If you believe I can really drive or really see, get in the car with me and we’ll see what happens to us at the end of the day,” he said, prompting laughter from the audience.

Check out the moment here:

Stevie Wonder had a message for the blindness skeptics during his show at Chicago's United Center on November 21: 

"If you believe I can really drive or really see, get in the car with me." pic.twitter.com/TDWVq804q7 

— Pigeons & Planes (@PigsAndPlans) November 23, 2026 

Wonder, who lost his sight shortly after birth, has addressed the speculation on numerous occasions, including during an emotional speech at a concert in Cardiff last summer .

“Seriously, you know the truth,” he told the crowd. “Truth is, shortly after my birth, I became blind.”

He went on to describe his blindness as a blessing that had allowed him to appreciate people for who they are rather than their physical appearance. “See people in the spirit of them, not how they look,” he continued. “Not what colour they are, but what colour is their spirit?”

In 2019, Wonder’s friend and fellow Motown star Lionel Richie recalled an occasion when the singer had played a practical…
items.t: Stevie Wonder addresses conspiracy theory that he’s not really blind: “Get in the car with me and we’ll see”

items.title: ‘God Of War’ actor Deborah Ann Woll reprises Laufey role for Amazon adaptation
items.summary:
Deborah Ann Woll will be reprising her role as Faye in the God Of War live-action adaptation at Amazon.

READ MORE: The “miracle” of ‘God Of War’s music – 20 years since the first game 

According to a report from Deadline , Ann Woll has joined the cast of God Of War , playing the wife of Dave Bautista’s Kratos.

Deborah Ann Woll played Faye in the 2018 reboot of God Of War and appears throughout 2022’s God Of War: Ragnarok in flashbacks, following her death at the start of the previous game.

Originally Amazon Prime Video’s God Of War series was going to star the game’s Thor actor Ryan Hurst as Kratos until an on-set injury forced him to be recast . Dave Bautista will now play the titular God Of War . Filming is currently taking place, after Amazon was forced to scrap all their previously-shot scenes.

God Of War has been given a two series order at Amazon, though it doesn’t currently have a release date.

‘God Of War: Laufey’. CREDIT: Sony Santa Monica 
 Kratos game actor Christopher Judge was in talks to reprise his role in the series before ultimately deciding to pass on the project. “I thought, ‘God, what a great legacy to leave for my grandson.’ So I started working out. I got bigger. I did read for it [but] it was so hard for me to memorise my lines, which I never had a problem with [before]. And that was my mind and body starting to tell me, ‘You don’t want to do this’,” he explained.

Deborah Ann Woll is set to return as Faye in spin-off game God Of War: Laufey , which is now set to launch May 20, 2027 after being delayed from February .

items.title: Ed Sheeran fans claim they were denied entry to Chile concert for wearing Palestine-linked football shirts
items.summary:
Fans of Ed Sheeran have claimed they were initially denied entry to his concert in Chile over the weekend for wearing football shirts with links to Palestine.

READ MORE: Ed Sheeran – ‘Play’ review: a hasty retreat to the genre-spanning of old 

The singer played the first of two shows at the Estadio Bicentenario de La Florida in Santiago on Saturday (November 21) as part of his ongoing ‘Loop’ world tour.

In footage shared by Chilean news outlet El Periódico , two concertgoers claimed that security personnel had initially refused to allow them into the stadium because they were wearing clothing associated with Club Deportivo Palestino, a Chilean football team founded by Palestinian immigrants in 1920.

According to BioBioChile , the fans challenged security staff, pointing out that no such clothing restrictions had been included in the concert’s entry conditions. They were eventually allowed into the venue, but said they had missed the first three songs of Sheeran’s set.

The attendees described the incident as arbitrary discrimination, arguing that their clothing posed no security risk and constituted a legitimate expression of their personal and political identity.

items.title: D’Angelo’s posthumous ‘GTA 6’ anthem ‘Kamikazi’ hits streaming with more music on the way
items.summary:
D’Angelo ’s estate has released posthumous single ‘Kamikazi’ on streaming after it appeared on the Grand Theft Auto 6 soundtrack.

READ MORE: D’Angelo, 1974-2025: neo-soul trailblazer who made magic from the shadows 

Last October, D’Angelo’s family confirmed the neo-soul pioneer died after “a prolonged and courageous battle” with pancreatic cancer . 

However, unreleased track ‘Kamikazi’ was included in Grand Theft Auto 6 ’s in-game Worldwide radio station and yesterday (November 23) D’Angelo’s estate shared the track on streaming .

“Michael approved this track in its current form in November of 2024 to be released as part of Grand Theft Auto 6,” he brother Luther Archer Jr said in a statement. “He was a tremendous admirer of Rockstar Games and a past collaborator of theirs. He was enthusiastic (to say the least) to have this record included in the game and released to a wide audience as a single.”

View this post on Instagram 

D’Angelo previously wrote ‘ Unshaken ’ for the Red Dead Redemption 2 soundtrack. According to Rockstar Games’ head of music Ivan Pavlovich, the musician would turn up at the game developer’s New York offices to play early versions of the game. “When D’Angelo comes through, he shows up at midnight, and he’s playing [ Red Dead Redemption 2 ] until four in the morning. Each time he was just like, ‘It’s incredible.’ It just blows his mind. He’s such a fan. I have never seen someone that excited,” Pavlovich said in an interview with Rolling Stone . 

A vinyl edition of ‘Kamikazi’ is also available to pre-order .

In July 2023, NME announced our return to print with a bi-monthly global magazine that showcases the best new artists and bands on earth, alongside exclusive new franchises, unmissable features, industry insight and expert reviews of the latest music, TV, film, and gaming releases.

Artists who have graced the print cover since include ENHYPEN , Laufey , The Last Dinner Party , Chappell Roan , Kneecap , LE SSERAFIM , Nemahsis , Oklou , Kwn , Waylon Wyatt , Rose Gray and Yves . All editions have sold out in minutes, which is why you should mark your calendar for the November/December 2026 issue, which will go on sale this Thursday November 26 at 2pm GMT. items.title: ‘Focker-In-Law’ is getting destroyed by critics: “Downright painful”
items.summary:
Focker-In-Law , the fourth film in the Meet The Parents series, is being mauled by critics.

READ MORE: ‘Focker-In-Law’ review: Even Ariana Grande’s comedy chops can’t save this legacy sequel 

The original Meet The Parents was released in 2000 and spawned two sequels (2005’s Meet The Fockers and 2010’s Little Fockers ) before a 16-year break. Later this week, the fourth film in the series, Focker-In-Law , hits cinema screens.

“Henry (Skyler Gisondo), son of Greg ( Ben Stiller ) and Pam Focker (Teri Polo), aims to marry Olivia ( Ariana Grande ), a strong-willed former hostage negotiator who appears to be his complete mismatch. To Greg’s shock, father-in-law Jack Byrnes ( Robert De Niro ) takes a liking to Olivia, and her unprecedented rise into his Circle of Trust sparks chaos in the family before Jack’s 80th birthday party,” reads the official logline.

Yesterday (November 23) reviews for the legacy sequel went live and critics aren’t impressed. Focker-In-Law currently has a 23 per cent rating on review aggregate site Rotten Tomatoes .

“It’s downright painful watching Robert De Niro, one of our greatest actors, and Ben Stiller, who’s capable of so much more, reprising the same formulaic shtick. The comic set pieces, of which there are many, nearly all revolve around humiliation, with Stiller painfully going through the motions as his character does one moronic thing after another,” reads The Hollywood Reporter ’s two-star review.

“It’s a painful and pointless experience, which refuses to come to any new conclusions about these characters, other than making them learn…

items.title: ‘My name was poison’: Donny Osmond on fame, failure – and his friend Michael Jackson
items.summary:
He was the child star of the Osmonds who become a global celebrity by 14. Then, at 21, his career came crashing down. Here, he reveals how he survived his years in exile – and what happened when Jackson was accused of child abuse

For a brief period in the early 1970s, Donny Osmond ruled the world. He was the global teenage heart-throb. Even Michael Jackson trailed behind him. He was 14 when his most famous song, Puppy Love, spent five weeks at No 1 in the UK. My sister had a huge poster of him on her bedroom wall. Then again, everybody’s sister had a poster of him on their bedroom wall. Between 1972 and 1973 he had six Top 5 hits in the UK, three of them No 1s (including The Twelfth of Never and Young Love). He was equally successful back home in the US.

Osmond was clean-cut, religious and respectful, with a mighty ability to punch out cover versions of saccharine standards. From his purple velvet cap to his doleful eyes and dazzling all-American smile, he was a marketing dream. We’d only just finished with Beatlemania. And now there was Donnymania.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘My name was poison’: Donny Osmond on fame, failure – and his friend Michael Jackson

Try as one might to resist comparison, the balance of this particular yin and yang has been shifting for some time. Twelve months ago, when Interpol and Bloc Party announced a UK and European co-headline tour, the pairing looked like an even contest: two of 00s indie’s most revered acts, whose landmark debuts remain touchstones of the era.

Since then, their fortunes have diverged. As an opening bass drone strafes the room, Bloc Party arrive in Cardiff in superficially fine, if puzzling, form. Their seventh album, Anatomy of a Brief Romance, has been met with diminishing returns, its Snapchat-caption triteness – “Every day is such a vibe”, runs one refrain – and creative inertia doing little to win over listeners.

items.title: Fontaines DC review – thrilling gothic grandeur from a band vaulting into greatness
items.summary:
M&S Bank Arena, Liverpool
Just a few years since playing little dive bars, the Irish rockers have confidently scaled up to huge rooms like this – and are now one of the key interpreters of modern malaise

A mere seven years since their debut, Dogrel, Fontaines DC have enjoyed a virtually seamless passage from Dublin dive bars to arenas, with stadiums to follow next year. Each step has been taken seemingly effortlessly in their stride and this latest outing is no exception. Bathed in shimmering blue light, the band are well into hymnal opener Six Shot Morning before we even see sight of singer Grian Chatten. He wanders on while singing, an entrance worthy of Frank Sinatra.

Chatten has previously seemed to distrust showbiz, but if anything the singer seems far more comfortable on the bigger stage than he ever did on smaller ones. With his Korn T-shirt, unfeasibly baggy trousers and tiny tattoo reading “deadly” in capitals, he leaps around, raises his arms to whip up the crowd and points the microphone towards them to sing key lines. Similarly, music this intense, dark, elegiac and even bleak – which speaks to the void at the heart of much modern life – is hardly typical arena fare but works brilliantly by taking on a more anthemic, celebratory aspect. It’s certainly weirdly thrilling hearing Chatten’s lines such as “We’re all depressed, running on a wheel” or “I don’t feel anything in the modern world” – or a song as plainly dark as Jackie Down the Line – become enormous, arena-uniting sing-songs.
items.t: Fontaines DC review – thrilling gothic grandeur from a band vaulting into greatness

items.title: The week’s best new tracks and the act you need to know: the rangy folk-prog songwriting of Threshold
items.summary:
Isaac Eiger’s solo venture leaves jangle pop behind for a wilder sound. Often it owes a debt to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days?

From New York via Montana
Recommended if you like Cameron Winter, Tobias Jesso Jr, Alex G
Up next Supporting Caroline on tour in Canada and the US until 19 November

Isaac Eiger is something of a scene legend in the world of American indie-rock. Raised in Bozeman, Montana, he was the founder and lead singer of the cult shoegaze-adjacent six-piece Strange Ranger, who left heartbroken a small, fervent fanbase when they announced their breakup in 2023. Taking a discernibly British approach to their sound, Strange Ranger traversed C86-y jangle-pop before landing on Madchester rave-up for their final album, 2023’s Pure Music. But Eiger is nothing if not musically worldly: he has written and produced with both underground heroes (Cassandra Jenkins, Chanel Beads) and nascent pop stars (Adéla, Frost Children).

Ever-prolific, Eiger also has a solo project under the name Threshold, with which he released a gauzy, 19-minute EP in 2024 called Thief. Earlier this year, he released Stillwater, the first single from the debut Threshold album, due for release in 2027 on the London-based label Untitled. Although Stillwater has some clear influences – it owes some phrasings and intonations to Alex G, but what indie-rock song doesn’t these days? – it’s still a remarkable song: expansive and…

items.title: The month’s best experimental album: Stella Z’s ambient adventures into lucid dreaming
items.summary:
(CDR)
Based around sounds recorded on her trips back to China, the Fujian-born, London-based producer creates a curious nocturnal collage on Thunder Is the Sky Dreaming

Lucid dreaming is one of the influences behind Thunder Is the Sky Dreaming, the new record from Fujian-born, London-based producer Stella Z. “Every night is an adventure,” she writes in the liner notes, “I can even smell things in certain dreams.” The eight tracks here are suitably sensory, scattered with effervescent sounds, ephemeral whispers and polyrhythmic percussion.

Many of the sounds and textures were recorded during trips back to China – the ambient noises of a pharmacy or the Fujian mountains late at night – a curious, collage-like approach that underpins the record. On The Somnium Is Awaiting My Cue, we hear what appear to be insects buzzing around a plodding bassline and sporadic woodwind motifs, while electronics softly spiral. Similarly hypnotic is Mira Miruna, on which the echoes of words gradually reveal themselves among the fizzing, softly discordant arrangement: a warped, increasingly urgent call to “wake up”, reminiscent of the foggy state as you rise from sleep. Z amplifies this heady feeling later on in Exit, Elsewhere, where her overlapping narration and rattling bells cause total disorientation.

items.title: Take That: Dreamers review – 50-something boyband fail to relight the fire on nostalgia-drenched return
items.summary:
(EMI)
The pallid disco revivalism sounds like S Club 7 and the folksy stomp-clap like Mumford and Sons – yet a few standout moments prove they can still strike gold if they try

Listening to Wonderkids, the string-laden opener of Take That’s new album, it seems the three remaining fiftysomething boybanders are feeling reflective. “Forgiving you, forgiving me / This vicious circle is now complete,” sings Gary Barlow.

In the years since their last record, the band – and former member Robbie Williams – have indeed laid out the trials and tribulations of 35 years of Take That in several documentaries, some more candid than others. Earlier this year, they even embarked on a revival of their blockbuster 2009 Circus tour. Unfortunately, all this reminiscing has left their 10th album feeling so steeped in nostalgia that any moments of greatness struggle for attention.

items.title: ‘We’re the most arrogant of all apes!’ A delightfully mind-expanding encounter with Peter Gabriel
items.summary:
From sampling to streaming, the rock legend has always been in thrall to technology – but is superintelligence a step too far? Back with an epic new album, he unpacks his remarkable ideas

Peter Gabriel asks me to fetch my laptop: he wants to show me a video of himself playing a keyboard duet with a bonobo called Kanzi. In fairness, said footage is, as Gabriel suggests, “extraordinary”. Working with primatologist Sue Savage-Rumbaugh, who developed a means of communicating with bonobos involving sign language and a speech-synthesis keyboard, Gabriel plays droning chords on a synthesiser while Kanzi picks out complementary notes on a piano. “Look, she likes that note, which is a ninth, and then she finds the octave,” he enthuses as the video plays. “There’s a real musicality there.”

It is all deeply unlikely, but it seems the perfect illustration of how easily a conversation with Gabriel can go wildly – if fascinatingly – off-piste. I’ve only been in his company for 10 minutes, long enough to ask a solitary question about his epic new album o\i: its 13 tracks last nearly 90 minutes, the result, he suggests, of a longstanding interest in African music “which made me realise that a song could last as long as a song could last”, and of “being old enough to think ‘fuck it’, really”. For anyone who feels that an hour and a half of exquisitely arranged, beautifully produced, occasionally deeply strange art rock – its sound shapeshifting from the folk-flecked A Hard Lesson to the glowing pop hues of Till Your Mind Is Shining – is too meagre an offering, it arrives in…
